rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: To evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Lease expiration or a change in ownership is not just cause, and removing housing services such as parking, storage or laundry also requires just cause.
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes; must be dominant motive
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. This includes some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits: units that first got a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979, tenancies eligible for rent increases under Costa-Hawkins, and some units whose rent is regulated by another government agency.
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance; this page does not list those exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unit must be covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions; the specific exemptions from coverage are not stated on this page.

rules.penalty: A landlord who evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.conflict_note: The page does not state an effective date. It cites 'Ordinance Section 37.9(a)'; the Rent Ordinance is Chapter 37 of the SF Administrative Code.
